candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16: identify medication precautions/contraindications, adverse effects, and safe administration
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — bevacizumab perioperative wound-healing precaution
candidate.educational_objective: Apply the labeled perioperative bevacizumab safety rule: withhold AVASTIN for at least 28 days before elective surgery because of wound-healing complications.

options.A: Withhold bevacizumab for at least 28 days before the elective surgery
options.B: Continue bevacizumab through the day of surgery because it does not affect wound healing
options.C: Hold bevacizumab only on the morning of surgery
options.D: Increase the bevacizumab dose before surgery to reduce postoperative bleeding

candidate.rationale: AVASTIN is associated with surgery and wound-healing complications. Current labeling instructs clinicians to withhold AVASTIN for at least 28 days before elective surgery. It also states not to administer AVASTIN for at least 28 days following major surgery and until adequate wound healing. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Bevacizumab should be withheld for at least 28 days before elective surgery because of surgery/wound-healing complications; post-major-surgery administration is also delayed until at least 28 days and adequate healing.
candidate.source_locator: §2.1 Dosage and Administration: withhold for at least 28 days prior to elective surgery; do not administer for at least 28 days following major surgery and until adequate wound healing; §5.2 Surgery and Wound Healing Complications
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
candidate.stem: A client receiving bevacizumab (AVASTIN) is scheduled for elective major surgery. Which preoperative medication plan is consistent with the current prescribing information?
